item.title: Stablecoins Are Becoming Financial Infrastructure — Not Just Crypto Infrastructure
item.description: Stablecoins have moved from a crypto-trading tool to real payment rails for remittances, payroll, and treasury. Here's what changed, and what hasn't.

item.title: Ethereum vs. Solana: What Are Developers Actually Building On?
item.description: A practical look at where developers actually build — DeFi, tokenization, consumer apps — and the tradeoffs that drive the choice between Ethereum and Solana.

item.title: Why Wall Street Keeps Launching Crypto Exchange-Traded Funds
item.description: What asset managers keep launching crypto ETFs for, what an ETF wrapper gives up versus holding crypto directly, and what it signals about adoption.

item.title: Crypto Wallets Are Getting Easier to Use. Is the Seed Phrase Era Ending?
item.description: How account abstraction, passkeys, and social recovery are replacing the seed phrase as crypto wallets' default onboarding experience, and the tradeoffs.

item.title: What Is a Blockchain Node — and Why Does Decentralization Depend on Them?
item.description: A plain-English explainer on what a blockchain node is, how it differs from a validator or miner, and why node count and distribution drive decentralization.

item.title: Tokenization Is Growing Fast. Does Everything Really Need a Token?
item.description: What tokenization actually adds versus a normal database, when putting an asset on-chain solves a real problem, and when it's a token for its own sake.

item.title: The Senate Votes on the CLARITY Act Tomorrow. It Should Pass.
item.description: The Senate holds a cloture vote on the CLARITY Act. ChainBrief makes the case for passage: the roadblocks, the key senators, and what betting markets price in.

item.title: Circle Built Its Own Blockchain. The Gas Token Is USDC.
item.description: Circle's Arc layer-1 launched with USDC as its gas token, a permissioned validator set including BlackRock and DTCC, and sub-second finality. Here's why.

item.title: Five Utility Tokens, Put to the Test
item.description: A skeptical, test-based look at five utility tokens — Chainlink, Filecoin, Helium, Render, Livepeer — asking whether each actually needs a token.

item.title: Voices to Know: The Web3 Growth Marketer Podcasting About the Part Nobody Livestreams
item.description: An introduction to Stefan Furcoi's Trust to Traction podcast, covering user trust, onboarding, and go-to-market strategy for wallets and protocols.

item.title: The CLARITY Act Failed. The SEC and CFTC Say They'll Regulate Crypto Anyway.
item.description: After the CLARITY Act's cloture vote failed, SEC Chair Paul Atkins and CFTC Chair Michael Selig said their agencies will pursue crypto rules regardless.

item.title: What Is a Cloture? And Is the CLARITY Act Dead, or Dead for Now?
item.description: A plain-English explainer on Senate cloture: why the CLARITY Act needed 60 votes, what happens after a failed vote, and whether the bill is really dead.

item.title: Aave, Morpho, and Uniswap Just Deployed on a Chain They Don't Control
item.description: DeFi protocols including Aave and Morpho deployed on Circle's permissioned Arc blockchain at launch. Here's why, and the tension with DeFi's permissionless roots.

item.title: Crypto Spent $206 Million on This Fight. It Lost Anyway. What Happens to That Money Now?
item.description: Crypto spent roughly $206 million backing the CLARITY Act, more than any other industry, and the bill still failed. Here's why, and what happens next.

item.title: The Two Senators Who Might Still Save the CLARITY Act
item.description: A profile of Sen. Ruben Gallego and Sen. Thom Tillis, the negotiators behind CLARITY's ethics compromise, and why their work may be its best path forward.

item.title: Why 18 State Attorneys General — Republicans and Democrats Alike — Wanted CLARITY Dead
item.description: An explainer on the bipartisan 18-state coalition that opposed CLARITY over federal preemption, the disputed 'qualified transaction' definition, and the stakes.

item.title: The SEC Just Let Real Stocks Trade on Public Blockchains
item.description: The SEC granted a five-year exemption letting real, dividend- and voting-rights-bearing U.S. shares trade on public blockchains. The mechanism, and who benefits.

item.title: The CFTC Sent Its Crypto Rulebook to the White House. Here's What That Actually Means.
item.description: The CFTC submitted a crypto market-structure proposal to the White House OMB after the Senate's failed CLARITY vote. What the submission means, and what's next.

item.title: Twenty-One of the World's Biggest Banks Are Building Their Own Stablecoin
item.description: A 21-bank consortium including Bank of America, Citi, and Goldman Sachs is forming a venture to issue a dollar stablecoin, targeting a 2027 launch.

item.title: A Hacker Drained $319 Million From a Bitcoin Network, Then Gave Most of It Back
item.description: A caching bug let an attacker mint unbacked bitcoin and withdraw $319 million from Liquid Network. About 85% came back after a patch. Here's what happened.

item.title: Crypto's Midterm War Chest Now Has AI and Sports Betting Money Behind It
item.description: New reporting shows crypto, AI, and sports-betting super PACs have committed more than $500 million to the 2026 midterms. The numbers, and the CLARITY tie-in.

item.title: What Is "Exemptive Relief," and Why Is the SEC Using It Instead of Writing New Rules?
item.description: A plain-language explainer on SEC exemptive relief: what it is, how it differs from rulemaking, its history with products like ETFs, and why it's everywhere now.

item.title: Real-World Asset Tokenization Just Crossed $34 Billion. Here's What That Actually Means.
item.description: The on-chain real-world asset market reached $34.18 billion, with tokenized equities up 390% year-to-date. What's actually growing, and what issuance hides.

item.title: Staking Finally Showed Up Inside a U.S. Crypto ETF
item.description: Grayscale's Ethereum ETF began distributing staking rewards, a first for a U.S.-listed spot crypto fund. Canary Capital has filed a staked SEI ETF too.

item.title: Wall Street Found a Way Into Prediction Markets Without Touching the Bets Themselves
item.description: ETF provider Tema launched a fund holding equity stakes in Kalshi and Polymarket rather than their contracts, sidestepping ongoing SEC scrutiny.

item.title: What's Actually Driving This Month's Layer-2 and DeFi Rally
item.description: Layer-2 and DeFi tokens posted some of the year's sharpest gains. A look at the specific catalysts, and which ones are actually load-bearing.

item.title: The Fed Just Wrote the Actual Rulebook for Stablecoins
item.description: The Fed proposed capital, reserve, and two-day redemption rules for GENIUS Act stablecoin issuers — the operational detail behind the 2026 law.

item.title: The SEC's Quiet End-Run Around a Stalled Congress
item.description: The SEC proposed "Regulation Crypto Assets," a securities-law framework with new offering exemptions and a safe harbor — built without waiting on Congress.

item.title: FinCEN Just Put a Number on Crypto Scam Losses: $13 Billion
item.description: FinCEN found almost $13 billion linked to crypto investment scams across all 50 states — far more than 2026's on-chain hacks have cost combined.

item.title: The Race for a Federal Crypto Bank Charter Is Quietly Ending
item.description: Circle, Ripple, Paxos, BitGo, and Crypto.com have all won OCC national trust bank charters in 2026 — federally regulated custody, without the ability to take deposits.

item.title: Wall Street's Biggest Futures Exchange Now Trades Crypto Like Crypto
item.description: CME Group's crypto futures and options now trade 24/7 — closing the weekend gap that has separated regulated derivatives from crypto-native exchanges.

item.title: What 15 of the World's Biggest Investors Actually Think About Crypto
item.description: Bitwise's first institutional crypto report: 15 major investors held or added to Bitcoin through a 50% drawdown, and none cited price as a reason to sell.

item.title: Consumers Will Use Stablecoins — If They Feel Like a Bank Account
item.description: Visa's survey found stablecoin adoption intent rises from 36% to 56% with bank-level fraud protection and deposit insurance added.

item.title: AI Agents Are Starting to Pay Each Other in Stablecoins
item.description: AI agents are settling payments to each other in stablecoins via new protocols like x402 — machine-to-machine commerce with no human approving each transaction.

item.title: A Five-Year-Old Bug Just Cost Bitcoin Holders $116 Million
item.description: A 2021 firmware flaw in Coldcard hardware wallets weakened key randomness for years, letting an attacker steal roughly $116 million from over 5,200 addresses.

item.title: Crypto Hacks Hit a Record in 2026 — the Losses Didn't
item.description: 2026 crypto hack losses hit $2.2B across 288 attacks — but a small number of huge breaches, not typical exploits, account for most of the money lost.
